List Target product questions and answers. Lists customer questions for a Target item given by its numeric 'tcin', each with its text, author, submission time, helpful votes and nested answers. 'page' is zero-based and 'per_page' runs 1 to 25. The response gives 'total_pages' and 'count' for paging.

### `target_reviews`

List Target product reviews. Lists written reviews for a Target item given by its numeric 'tcin'. Each review has its rating, title, text, author, submission time, helpful votes, and verified and syndicated flags. 'page' is zero-based and stops at 50; 'per_page' runs 1 to 25. The response gives 'total' and 'total_pages'.

### `target_search`

Search Target products. Searches Target products and returns products plus every filter group and option available for the current result set. Pass option ids back through filter_ids as a comma-separated list. A zero total with an empty products list is a valid no-results response. The sort enum accepts 'relevance', 'featured', 'price-low', 'price-high', 'rating', 'bestselling', and 'newest'.

### `target_stores`

Find Target stores near a location. Returns Target's physical stores near a ZIP code, a free-text "city, state", or a "latitude,longitude" pair, including each store's store_id, status, distance, phone, address, service list, time zone, and two weeks of daily opening hours. Use the returned store_id values with the store_id parameter on target-search, target-category-products, target-filter-options, and target-product.

### `tcgplayer_filters`

List the printing, condition and language filters of a TCGplayer product line. Returns the values the tcgplayer-sales filters accept for one TCGplayer product line: the printings (variants such as Normal, Foil, Holofoil or 1st Edition), the six conditions, the languages and the listing types, each with TCGplayer's id. Printings belong to one product line (Pokemon has Reverse Holofoil, Magic has Foil), while languages are shared. Give product_line (a url_name from tcgplayer-product-lines) or id (a TCGplayer product id, which uses that product's line). An unknown product line returns invalid parameters and an unknown product returns not found.

### `tcgplayer_listings`

List the sellers offering a TCGplayer product. Returns one page of the current seller listings for a TCGplayer product: seller storefront name, rating and sales volume, condition, printing, language, quantity, price, shipping price and seller location. Filter by condition, printing and language, and sort by price or price with shipping.

### `tcgplayer_price_guide`

Get TCGplayer's price guide for a whole set. Returns TCGplayer's price guide for one set, one row per card, condition and printing: card id, name, collector number, rarity, condition, printing, language, low price, market price and units sold. Page through a whole set (up to 500 rows per call) instead of fetching each card; the set_id comes from tcgplayer-sets.

### `tcgplayer_price_history`

Get a TCGplayer product's price history. Returns a TCGplayer product's price history over a month, quarter, half year or year, per condition, printing and language: market price, quantity sold, transaction count and low/high sale price for each period, plus the average daily sales volume.

### `tcgplayer_product`

Get a TCGplayer product's detail and price points. Returns one TCGplayer product in full: name, product line, set, rarity, card number, card text, attributes, the market, lowest and median prices, listing and seller counts, every purchasable condition/variant/language SKU, and TCGplayer's market and buylist price per printing.

### `tcgplayer_product_lines`

List TCGplayer product lines. Lists TCGplayer's product lines (games and product families such as Pokemon, Magic: The Gathering, Yu-Gi-Oh!, One Piece and Lorcana): id, name and the url_name that tcgplayer-search and tcgplayer-sets take as product_line.

### `tcgplayer_sales`

Get a TCGplayer product's most recent sales. Returns the five most recent completed sales of a TCGplayer product: condition, printing, language, quantity, sale price, shipping price and order time. Optionally restrict to one condition (near-mint, lightly-played, moderately-played, heavily-played, damaged or unopened), one printing (variant such as Normal, Foil or Reverse Holofoil), one language (such as English or Japanese) and whether the listing had photos. The printing and language values a product accepts come from tcgplayer-filters; an unlisted value returns invalid parameters. A variant or language filter makes one extra call to read the product line's filter values.

### `tcgplayer_search`

Search TCGplayer trading-card products. Searches TCGplayer's catalog of trading-card and collectible products (Pokemon, Magic, Yu-Gi-Oh!, One Piece, Lorcana and about 70 other product lines) and returns one page of matches: product id, name, set, rarity, card number, market, lowest and median prices, listing count, links and filter facets. Filter by product line, set, product type, rarity, card type and price range, and sort by price, listings, sales or name.

### `tcgplayer_sets`

List the sets of a TCGplayer product line. Lists the active sets (expansions) of one TCGplayer product line, newest first: name, the url_name that tcgplayer-search takes as set, abbreviation and release date.

### `techcrunch_article`

Get TechCrunch article content. Returns public TechCrunch article metadata (title, author(s), published/updated dates, dek, section, lead image) and body paragraphs from a canonical article URL.

### `techcrunch_author`

Get a TechCrunch author profile. Returns one TechCrunch staff writer or contributor's public profile: name, job title, headshot, biography, social links, and one page of their recent articles.

### `techcrunch_headlines`

Get TechCrunch category headlines. Returns the latest TechCrunch stories for one category. 'section' is required and takes one of 22 slugs such as 'artificial-intelligence', 'startups', 'venture', 'security', 'fintech', 'space' or 'cryptocurrency'. Each item has its title, URL, summary, publication time and author.

### `techcrunch_news`

Get TechCrunch top stories. Returns the latest TechCrunch top stories from its home feed. Takes no parameters. Each item has its title, URL, summary, publication time and author name.

### `techcrunch_sections`

Get TechCrunch categories. Lists the 22 TechCrunch categories that 'techcrunch-headlines' accepts, taken from the site's primary navigation dropdown. Each entry has a stable 'slug', a display 'name' and the category's feed 'url'. For example, 'artificial-intelligence' is named AI.

### `techradar_article`

Get TechRadar article content. Returns a TechRadar article by canonical 'url' on 'techradar.com': title, description, section, authors, publication and update times, lead image, the body 'paragraphs' and a 'paywalled' flag.

### `techradar_author`

Get a TechRadar author profile. Returns a TechRadar author's profile, looked up by 'slug' (for example 'tom-power') or canonical 'url', which may end in '/page/<n>'; exactly one is required. 'page' (1-based, default 1) overrides any page in 'url'. The response has the name, 'job_title', biography, social links, one page of articles and 'has_next_page'.

### `techradar_headlines`

Get TechRadar section headlines. Returns the latest TechRadar stories for one section hub. 'section' is required and takes one of 25 slugs such as 'computing', 'phones', 'audio', 'gaming', 'deals', 'reviews', 'news' or 'vpn'. Each item has its title, URL, summary, publication time, author and image.

### `techradar_news`

Get TechRadar top stories. Returns TechRadar's latest top stories across the site. Takes no parameters, and 'techradar-headlines' narrows by section instead. Each item has its title, URL, summary, publication time, author and image.

### `techradar_sections`

Get TechRadar sections. Lists the 25 top-level TechRadar sections that 'techradar-headlines' accepts, such as 'computing', 'phones', 'best', 'deals' and 'how-to'. Each entry has a 'slug', a display 'name' and the section page 'url'.

### `telegram_bot`

Get a public Telegram bot's profile. Returns a public Telegram bot's profile from its t.me page: name, verified flag, description, avatar link and, when Telegram shows it, the number of monthly users. username is the bot's public username, with or without a leading @ or a t.me URL prefix. A channel, group, person's account or invite link is reported as such so you can use the right endpoint; an unknown username returns not found. Only public profile text is read.

### `telegram_channel`

Get a public Telegram channel profile. Returns the public profile of a Telegram channel: title, description, verification badge, subscriber count, and the photo, video, file and link counters shown on the channel's public web preview (t.me/s/{username}). username is the channel's public username, with or without a leading @ or a t.me link; private channels, groups, bots, user accounts and invite links are not supported and return an error that says which kind of name was given. subscribers is the exact figure when available; subscribers_approximate is true when only the preview's abbreviated figure (for example 10.3M) could be read. The photo, video, file and link counters are the preview's abbreviated figures and are approximate for large channels. Only public content is read, no media files are returned, and Telegram's terms restrict using platform content to train AI or machine-learning systems, so results must not be used for that purpose.

### `telegram_channel_posts`

List posts from a public Telegram channel. Returns one page of up to 20 posts from a public Telegram channel's web preview (t.me/s/{username}), newest first. Each post has its id, link, text, links found in the text, publish time, edited flag, view count, author signature, forwarded-from and reply references, photo and video thumbnails, link-preview card, and reaction tallies. Page backwards by passing the previous response's next_before as before; has_more is false and next_before is omitted on the last page. Pass query to search inside the channel instead of browsing; search pages use the same before cursor. A search with no matches returns an empty posts list. Views are the preview's abbreviated figures (for example 32.4K) and are approximate above 1,000. Media entries carry thumbnail references only, never playable file URLs. Polls, documents, voice notes and stickers appear as an unsupported media entry. Private channels, groups, bots, user accounts and channels that disabled their web preview are not supported. Telegram's terms restrict using platform content to train AI or machine-learning systems, so results must not be used for that purpose.

### `telegram_group`

Get a public Telegram group profile. Returns the public profile of a Telegram group from its public t.me page: title, description, member count and, when Telegram shows it, the number of members online. username is the group's public username, with or without a leading @ or a t.me link. Only the profile is available for groups; their messages are not readable here. Channels (use telegram-channel), bots, user accounts and invite links are not supported and return an error that says which kind of name was given; a username nobody owns returns not found. online is 0 when Telegram shows no online figure. avatar_url is omitted for groups without a profile photo. Only public content is read, and Telegram's terms restrict using platform content to train AI or machine-learning systems, so results must not be used for that purpose.

### `telegram_post`

Get one public Telegram channel post. Returns a single post from a public Telegram channel by username and post id, as Telegram's public embed widget shows it: text, links, publish time, edited flag, views, author signature, forwarded-from and reply references, photo and video thumbnails, link-preview card, and reaction tallies. The post id is the number at the end of a post link (t.me/durov/531 has id 531) or the id field of telegram-channel-posts. A post that does not exist, was deleted, or belongs to a channel that is not public returns not found. Telegram's terms restrict using platform content to train AI or machine-learning systems, so results must not be used for that purpose.

### `telegraph_article`

Get The Telegraph article content. Returns one The Telegraph article by 'url', a canonical HTTPS article link. The response has the title, description, section, authors, publication and update times, image URL, body 'paragraphs' and a 'paywalled' flag. Access is intermittent, and subscriber-only or blocked pages return an error.

### `telegraph_author`

Get a Telegraph author profile. Returns a Telegraph author's profile by 'url', a canonical 'telegraph.co.uk/authors/<letter>/<range>/<name>/' link: name, job title, bio and recent articles with title, URL, excerpt and ISO-8601 'published_at'. 'job_title' can be empty for contributors without a masthead credit.

### `telegraph_headlines`

Get The Telegraph section headlines. Returns the current headlines for one The Telegraph section. 'section' is required and takes one of 'uk-news', 'world-news', 'politics', 'business', 'finance', 'technology', 'sport', 'culture', 'travel', 'lifestyle', 'health', 'science' or 'opinion'. Each item has its title and URL.

### `telegraph_news`

Get The Telegraph top stories. Returns the current top stories from The Telegraph. It takes no parameters. Each item has its title, URL and, where available, a summary, author, publication time, image URL and 'type'. It can return an error when The Telegraph declines the request.

### `telegraph_sections`

Get The Telegraph sections. Lists the The Telegraph sections that the headlines endpoint accepts, such as 'uk-news', 'world-news', 'politics', 'finance', 'culture' and 'opinion'. Each entry has a 'slug', a display 'name' and a section 'url'.

### `tes_job_detail`

Get a Tes teaching job. Returns detail for one job posting by its numeric id (the id field returned by tes-job-search): employer, location, salary, contract terms/types, dates, and application contact/URL, plus a short excerpt of the listing description rather than the full long-form HTML copy.

### `tes_job_employer`

Get a Tes jobs employer profile. Returns detail for one jobs employer profile by its numeric id (the trailing id in tes-job-detail's employer_url field, e.g. .../jobs/employer/epsom-college-1039424 -- the 1039424): name, location, school type/phase/funding status/gender/age range, an about description, its postal address, and every currently-open position listed on the employer's own profile page (id, title, url -- call tes-job-detail with each id for the full posting).

### `tes_job_search`

Search Tes teaching jobs. Searches Tes's (tes.com) teaching-jobs board. Returns listing facts (title, employer, location, salary, contract terms/types) plus a short excerpt of the listing description, not the full long-form job-description copy, and the same live faceted-search breakdown (position/subject/workplace category trees with counts, plus contract type/term counts) the real search page renders as its filter sidebar. location is a free-text place name (a UK town/city, an international city, or a bare country name) resolved to coordinates; omit for Tes's own default market, "United Kingdom". radius_miles selects the search radius around location. contract_type and contract_term are validated against Tes's own small, closed label sets. position, subject, and workplace are comma-separated filters -- Tes's own category labels are numerous and can change, so read a prior response's own facets.positions[].value (and facets.positions[].children[].value)/facets.subjects[].value/facets.workplaces[].children[].value for the live, current set rather than guessing. salary_min filters to jobs with an advertised salary at or above that amount (in the searched market's local currency); Tes's own filter panel offers only a minimum, no maximum.

### `tes_resource_detail`

Get a Tes teaching resource. Returns detail for one teaching resource by its numeric id (the id field returned by tes-resource-search). Descriptive facts (title, subject, age range, resource type, author, price, rating, licence label), a per-file attachment list (file type, size, and a preview thumbnail -- metadata only), and the most recent page of reviews are returned -- not the downloadable resource file itself.

### `tes_resource_search`

Search Tes teaching resources. Searches Tes's (tes.com) teaching-resources marketplace. Returns listing facts (title, author, price, rating, downloads) -- not full listing descriptions. query is optional: omit it (alone, or combined with key_stage/subject/on_sale) for pure filter-driven or fully unfiltered browsing. sort mirrors the real search page's own Sort by dropdown; key_stage and subject mirror its left-hand Refine by filters (both closed, validated enums taken from Tes's own facet taxonomy, and always resolved against Tes's own single GB-taxonomy regardless of country). country controls result currency/localisation only (confirmed live for all seven values); it does not change which key_stage/subject values are valid.

### `tes_resource_shop`

Get a Tes teaching-resources author shop. Returns detail for one teaching-resources author/seller shop by its username (from tes-resource-search/tes-resource-detail's author field, or the trailing path segment of author_url): display name, average rating, upload/view/download counts, a bio, and a page of that author's resource listing (id, title, price, thumbnail -- call tes-resource-detail with each id for subject/age-range/resource-type/rating/description). subject narrows the listing to one of the subject tabs shown on the shop's own page; these vary per author and are not a curated enum.

### `tes_school_search`

Search the Tes Schools Directory. Searches Tes's (tes.com) public Schools Directory by school name or location. Returns listing facts (name, logo, a short description, address) for each matching school/employer. Each result's id is the same employer id tes-job-employer accepts, so a caller can go straight from a name/location search to a full employer profile (school type/phase/funding status/gender/age range, and its currently-open positions) without first needing a job posting to discover the id.

### `tesla_jobs_job`

Tesla Jobs single posting. Returns one Tesla Careers posting by its numeric job id (the 'id' field returned by the list endpoint).

### `tesla_jobs_list`

Tesla Jobs listing. Searches Tesla's public careers site (tesla.com/careers) via its own careers-state JSON endpoint. Tesla's own endpoint always returns its entire global job dataset regardless of query parameters; this filters and paginates that snapshot server-side. Listings carry identity/department/location metadata only — call the job endpoint for the full description, responsibilities, and requirements.

### `theage_article`

Get The Age article content. Returns one The Age article's public metadata and the body paragraphs an anonymous visitor's page request is served, from a canonical article URL. The Age runs a metered subscription paywall; the response reports it with is_accessible_for_free (the page's own declaration), paywalled (the page marks the story as subscriber content), and is_truncated (the page served a shortened preview, or no body at all, instead of the full story). Paywalls are never bypassed and body text is never fabricated. Video-only pages are rejected with a 400.

### `theage_author`

Get an Age journalist profile. Returns an Age journalist's public profile -- name, short biography, headshot, contact email and social links where published -- plus their recent stories, from a canonical https://www.theage.com.au/by/<name>-<id> URL.

### `theage_headlines`

Get The Age section headlines. Returns the current stories for one The Age section: title, canonical URL, summary, author, publication time, and image where the section lists them. section must be one of the slugs returned by /theage/sections; any other value is rejected with a 400 before The Age is contacted.

### `theage_news`

Get The Age top stories. Returns The Age's current "Latest News" public RSS feed: each story's title, canonical URL, summary, author, publication time, and lead image.

### `theage_sections`

Get The Age sections. Lists every The Age section accepted by /theage/headlines (96 sections from the site's own section menu), each with its slug, display name, and public section-front URL.

### `theatlantic_article`

Get an Atlantic article's content. Returns one public Atlantic article's metadata and body paragraphs from a canonical article URL. 'metered' reflects the site's own soft-paywall flag for that article; the body returned here is the same one the site's own page serves to an anonymous visitor and is never truncated because of it. An article whose page genuinely withholds its body is reported as a restricted-access error instead of a hollow response.

### `theatlantic_author`

Get an Atlantic staff author profile. Returns one Atlantic staff author's public profile -- name, headshot, and biography -- plus their recent articles, from a canonical author URL.

### `theatlantic_headlines`

Get the latest stories in an Atlantic section. Returns the current front-page article cards for one Atlantic section: each story's title, canonical URL, description, byline, publication time, and lead image. Section must be a slug returned by /theatlantic/sections.

### `theatlantic_sections`

List The Atlantic sections. Lists every top-level Atlantic section accepted by /theatlantic/headlines, with its slug, display name, and landing-page URL. Values: 'ideas', 'politics', 'economy', 'international', 'national-security', 'technology', 'science', 'health', 'education', 'culture', 'family', 'books', 'photography'.

### `theblaze_article`

Get a Blaze Media article. Returns one TheBlaze (Blaze Media) article by 'url', a canonical HTTPS editorial or show-story link on 'theblaze.com'; non-editorial paths and off-site URLs are rejected. The response has the title, description, section, authors, publication and update times, image URL, body 'paragraphs' and a 'paywalled' flag.

### `theblaze_author`

Get a Blaze Media contributor profile. Returns a public /u/<slug> profile and up to 30 recent article feed items. Provide exactly one of slug or canonical profile URL.

### `theblaze_headlines`

Get Blaze Media section headlines. Returns up to 30 recent stories from one TheBlaze (Blaze Media) section. 'section' is required, case-sensitive and must match exactly, for example 'news', 'columns/opinion', 'lifestyle/men', 'tech' or a show such as 'shows/relatable'. Other values are rejected. Items have a title and URL, plus summary, author, publication time and image when the outlet provides them.

### `theblaze_news`

Get Blaze Media top stories. Returns the latest site-wide stories from TheBlaze (Blaze Media), up to 30 items, covering news and opinion. Each item has a headline, canonical URL, publication time, byline, summary and image URL when published. It takes no parameters.

### `theblaze_sections`

List Blaze Media sections. Returns all verified article-bearing editorial and show sections accepted by the headlines endpoint. The contributors collection is included; the off-site Profile feed is excluded.

### `thebodyshop_collection_products`

List The Body Shop collection products. Returns products from one The Body Shop (https://www.thebodyshop.com) collection. The storefront URL is fixed; 'handle' is the collection's URL slug.

### `thebodyshop_collections`

List The Body Shop collections. Returns collections from The Body Shop (https://www.thebodyshop.com). The storefront URL is fixed. Valid empty result pages return '200' with an empty collections array.

### `thebodyshop_page`

Get a The Body Shop static page. Returns one The Body Shop static page by its 'handle': id, title, URL, plain-text 'content' and the created, published and updated timestamps. Page text is cleaned, not raw HTML. An unknown handle returns 404. When the reduced form is served, 'transport_mode' is 'ssr_embedded' and 'id' is omitted.

### `thebodyshop_pages`

List The Body Shop static pages. Lists The Body Shop static pages, 50 per request by default ('limit' up to 250), with 'page' starting at 1. Each page has its handle, title, URL, plain-text content and timestamps. An empty result is a normal 200. When 'transport_mode' is 'ssr_embedded', items carry only 'handle', 'url' and 'updated_at'.

### `thebodyshop_product`

Get a The Body Shop product. Returns product detail for one The Body Shop (https://www.thebodyshop.com) product handle. The storefront URL is fixed server-side; 'handle' is the product's URL slug.

### `thebodyshop_product_recommendations`

List The Body Shop product recommendations. Returns recommended products for one The Body Shop (https://www.thebodyshop.com) product handle. The storefront URL is fixed server-side.

### `thebodyshop_products`

List The Body Shop products. Returns products from The Body Shop's (https://www.thebodyshop.com) public product catalog. The storefront URL is fixed server-side. Valid empty result pages return '200' with an empty products array.

### `thebodyshop_search_suggest`

Get The Body Shop search suggestions. Returns products, collections, and query suggestions from The Body Shop's (https://www.thebodyshop.com) predictive search. The storefront URL is fixed server-side.

### `thebodyshop_sitemap_urls`

List The Body Shop sitemap URLs. Returns capped URL entries from The Body Shop's (https://www.thebodyshop.com) child sitemaps matching the requested type. The storefront URL is fixed server-side.

### `thebodyshop_sitemaps`

List The Body Shop sitemaps. Returns child sitemap URLs from The Body Shop's (https://www.thebodyshop.com) '/sitemap.xml' index with inferred sitemap types. The storefront URL is fixed server-side.

### `thebodyshop_store`

Get The Body Shop store metadata. Returns storefront metadata for The Body Shop (https://www.thebodyshop.com). The storefront URL is fixed server-side, so no 'url' parameter is accepted.

### `thedailybeast_article`

Get The Daily Beast article content. Returns one The Daily Beast article by its canonical 'url', either a root-level slug or one under a single content vertical such as 'obsessed'. The response has the title, description, section, authors, publication and update times, lead image URL, body 'paragraphs' and a 'paywalled' flag. Digest or index pages are not articles and return an error.

### `thedailybeast_author`

Get a The Daily Beast author profile. Returns one The Daily Beast reporter's public profile: name, job title, biography, headshot, social link, and their recent articles, from a canonical author URL.

### `thedailybeast_headlines`

Get The Daily Beast section headlines. Returns the current headlines of one The Daily Beast section. 'section' is required and takes a slug such as 'politics', 'politics/opinion', 'obsessed/reviews', 'scouted/home' or 'world/china'. Each item can carry its title, URL, summary, author, publication time, lead image and 'type', and the response echoes the 'section'.

### `thedailybeast_news`

Get The Daily Beast top stories. Returns the current top stories from The Daily Beast. It takes no parameters. Each item has its title, URL, summary, publication time, author and lead image, so it is a quick front-page view; use the headlines endpoint with a 'section' slug for one category.

### `thedailybeast_sections`

Get The Daily Beast sections. Lists the sections of The Daily Beast that the headlines endpoint accepts, both top-level categories such as 'politics' and 'world' and child sub-sections such as 'politics/opinion' and 'world/middle-east'. Each entry has a 'slug', a display 'name' and the section 'url'.

### `thehill_article`

Get The Hill article content. Returns one The Hill article by 'url', which must be a canonical HTTPS 'thehill.com' article link containing a numeric article id. The response has the title, description, section, authors, publication and update times, lead image URL, body 'paragraphs' and a 'paywalled' flag.

### `thehill_author`

Get a The Hill author profile. Returns a The Hill author's profile by 'url', a canonical 'thehill.com/author/<slug>/' link: name, job title, bio, image URL and recent articles with title, URL, category and category URL. 'job_title' and 'image_url' may be missing, and each article's 'published_at' is relative text such as '10 hours ago', not a timestamp.

### `thehill_headlines`

Get The Hill section headlines. Returns the current headlines for one The Hill section. 'section' is required and takes one of 19 slugs, including 'home', 'policy', 'business', 'senate', 'national-security' and 'technology'. Each item has its title and URL, plus summary, author, publication time and image when the outlet provides them, and the response echoes the 'section'.

### `thehill_news`

Get The Hill top stories. Returns the current top stories from The Hill. It takes no parameters. Each item has its title, URL and, where the outlet gives them, a summary, author, publication time, image URL and 'type'. Use the headlines endpoint to read one section instead.

### `thehill_sections`

Get The Hill RSS sections. Lists the 19 The Hill section slugs that the headlines endpoint accepts, such as 'home', 'policy', 'senate', 'defense' and 'technology'. Each entry has the section 'slug', its display 'name' and its 'url'.

### `thehindu_article`

Get The Hindu article content. Returns public The Hindu article metadata and body paragraphs from a canonical article URL. A story The Hindu marks subscriber-only returns a permission error instead of a body.

### `thehindu_author`

Get a The Hindu author profile. Returns a The Hindu author's byline metadata, biography, contact/social links, and their most recent articles from a canonical author URL.

### `thehindu_headlines`

Get The Hindu section headlines. Returns the current headlines for one The Hindu section. 'section' is required and takes a slug such as 'news-national', 'opinion-editorial', 'business-markets', 'sport-cricket' or 'sci-tech-health'. Items carry the title, URL, summary, author, publication time and image, and the response echoes the 'section'.

### `thehindu_news`

Get The Hindu top stories. Returns the current stories from The Hindu's Latest News listing. It takes no parameters. Each item has its title, URL and, where available, a summary, author, publication time, image URL and 'type'. For a single desk such as cricket or business, use the headlines endpoint.

### `thehindu_sections`

Get The Hindu sections. Lists the The Hindu section slugs that the headlines endpoint accepts, covering news, opinion, business, sport, entertainment, sci-tech, education, life and style, society, books and food, for example 'news-national', 'sport-cricket' and 'food-recipes'. Each entry has a 'slug', 'name' and 'url'.

### `thejournal_article`

Get TheJournal.ie article content. Returns public TheJournal.ie article metadata and body paragraphs from a canonical article URL. Stories are served in full to anonymous readers, so paywalled is never set.

### `thejournal_author`

Get a TheJournal.ie author page. Returns one TheJournal.ie author's public archive page: name, numeric author id, and the most recent articles the first page lists.

### `thejournal_headlines`

Get TheJournal.ie section headlines. Returns current headlines from one public TheJournal.ie section listing page, with the story type label, summary and image when the page shows them.

### `thejournal_news`

Get TheJournal.ie top stories. Returns the latest TheJournal.ie stories across all sections. Each item has a title, canonical URL, short summary, publication time (RFC 3339, UTC) and lead image. Items carry no author byline; the article endpoint supplies it. It takes no parameters.

### `thejournal_sections`

Get TheJournal.ie sections. Lists the 22 TheJournal.ie sections that the headlines endpoint accepts, verified 2026-09-25: nine category pages such as 'irish', 'politics' and 'business', plus topic pages such as 'housing', 'courts', 'ukraine' and 'gaza'. Each entry has a 'slug', 'name' and listing page 'url'. Topic pages outside the site navigation are not served.

### `thenextweb_article`

Get The Next Web article content. Returns one The Next Web article by 'url', which must be a canonical HTTPS 'thenextweb.com/news/<slug>' link; off-site URLs and non-article paths are rejected. The response has the title, description, section, authors, publication and update times, image URL, body 'paragraphs' and a 'paywalled' flag.

### `thenextweb_author`

Get a The Next Web author profile. Returns a The Next Web author's name, image URL and the story cards on their archive page. Give 'slug' or a canonical 'thenextweb.com/author/<slug>' 'url'; 'slug' is required when 'url' is omitted. Each article has a title, URL, summary, author, image, 'type' and publication time.

### `thenextweb_headlines`

Get The Next Web section headlines. Returns the story cards of one The Next Web editorial section. 'section' is required and must be one of 'deep-tech', 'sustainability', 'ecosystems', 'data-security', 'fintech-ecommerce', 'future-of-work', 'startups-technology', 'investors-funding', 'government-policy' or 'corporates-innovation'; other values return a 400.

### `thenextweb_news`

Get The Next Web top stories. Returns the current top stories from The Next Web. It takes no parameters. Each item has the publisher's title, canonical URL, summary, publication time and author, plus the image URL when one is present.

### `thenextweb_sections`

Get The Next Web sections. Returns the ten editorial sections in The Next Web's current homepage navigation. Topic/tag archives, media, events and promotional categories are excluded.

### `therealreal_autocomplete`

Get The RealReal search-box suggestions. Returns The RealReal's own search-box typeahead suggestions for a partial query.

### `therealreal_categories`

Get The RealReal category browse taxonomy. Returns The RealReal's full category (taxon) browse taxonomy: every department, category, and subcategory, nested, with each entry's id (usable directly against search's category_id), permalink (usable directly against the category endpoint's path), and live matching item count. This is reference data that changes rarely, so responses are cached.

### `therealreal_category`

Browse The RealReal listings by category. Returns a page of The RealReal listings browsed by category (taxon) permalink path, e.g. women/handbags. Pass a previous response's next_after back as after to fetch the next page.

### `therealreal_collection`

Browse The RealReal listings by curated collection. Returns a page of The RealReal listings browsed by curated collection slug, e.g. on-sale-now -- sale campaigns, editor's picks, and similar merchandising collections distinct from category/designer browsing. Pass a previous response's next_after back as after to fetch the next page.

### `therealreal_collections`

Get The RealReal curated collection slugs. Returns The RealReal's full published set of curated editorial and sale-campaign collection slugs (e.g. on-sale-now, hermes-birkin-bag), each usable directly against the collection endpoint's own slug field. This is reference data that changes rarely, so responses are cached.

### `therealreal_conditions`

Get The RealReal condition-grading value space. Returns The RealReal's full authentication condition-grading scale: the closed 6-tier set (Pristine, Excellent, Very Good, Good, Fair, As Is) it defines, each with an id (usable directly against search's condition_id) and live matching item count. This is reference data that changes rarely, so responses are cached.

### `therealreal_designer`

Browse The RealReal listings by designer. Returns a page of The RealReal listings browsed by designer slug, e.g. gucci. Pass a previous response's next_after back as after to fetch the next page.

### `therealreal_designers`

Get The RealReal designer directory. Returns every designer The RealReal recognizes in one department (not just designers with currently active listings), each with an id (usable directly against search's designer_id) and slug (usable directly against the designer endpoint). The directory is segmented by department -- pass category to select one; the response's categories field lists every accepted value. This is reference data that changes rarely, so responses are cached.

### `therealreal_listing`

Get a The RealReal listing detail. Returns a single The RealReal listing: description, condition detail, category context, and measurements, plus the shared summary fields (name, designer, condition, price, images). Looked up by the listing's full product URL, as returned in a search/category/designer response's url field.

### `therealreal_search`

Search The RealReal luxury consignment listings. Searches The RealReal's authenticated luxury resale catalog by keyword, optionally combined with category, designer, condition-grade, and price-range filters, returning listing summaries (name, designer, condition, price, images) plus the total matching count and an opaque pagination cursor. Pass a previous response's next_after back as after to fetch the next page.

### `therealreal_similar`

Get The RealReal similar-item recommendations. Returns The RealReal's own "Similar Items" visual-similarity recommendations for one product, looked up by the product's numeric id (from any other The RealReal endpoint's listing response id field).

### `thestarmy_article`

Get The Star (Malaysia) article content. Returns public The Star (Malaysia) story metadata and body paragraphs from a canonical story URL. Metered and premium stories return only the public teaser paragraphs the server shows anonymous readers, flagged with paywalled; a story with no readable teaser returns a permission error.

### `thestarmy_author`

Get a The Star (Malaysia) author page. Returns one The Star (Malaysia) byline's public author page: display name, the public byline email, and their most recent stories.

### `thestarmy_headlines`

Get The Star (Malaysia) section headlines. Returns the current stories of one The Star (Malaysia) section page, usually 10 and up to 100 on column-style sections. 'section' is required, for example 'news-nation', 'latest-business', 'sport-badminton' or 'latest-food'. Items have a title and URL, and when the page shows them a 'type', summary, byline, image and publication time. Older stories are not paginated.

### `thestarmy_news`

Get The Star (Malaysia) top stories. Returns the current top stories on The Star (Malaysia) home page. It takes no parameters. Each item has a title and canonical URL, plus a short section label in 'type', a summary and a byline when the page shows them. 'published_at' is omitted here; the section headlines endpoint carries it.

### `thestarmy_sections`

Get The Star (Malaysia) sections. Lists the 94 The Star (Malaysia) sections that returned at least one story to an anonymous reader when checked on 2026-09-25, and that the headlines endpoint accepts. Examples are 'news-latest', 'latest-nation', 'business-smebiz' and 'sport-football'. Each entry has a 'slug', a 'name' and the section page 'url'.

### `theverge_article`

Get The Verge article content. Returns one The Verge article by 'url', a canonical HTTPS article link. The response has the title, description, section, authors, publication and update times, lead image URL, body 'paragraphs' and a 'paywalled' flag. Subscriber-only or blocked pages return an error instead.

### `theverge_author`

Get a The Verge author profile. Returns a The Verge author's profile by 'url', a canonical 'theverge.com/authors/<slug>' link: name, job title such as Senior Reporter, bio and recent articles. Each article has a title, URL, excerpt, ISO-8601 'published_at' and 'category', the post's primary Verge vertical such as Tech.

### `theverge_headlines`

Get The Verge section headlines. Returns the current headlines for one The Verge section. 'section' is required and takes one of 'tech', 'reviews', 'science', 'entertainment', 'ai', 'policy', 'gaming', 'mobile', 'apps' or 'features'. Each item has its title, URL, summary, author and publication time.

### `theverge_news`

Get The Verge top stories. Returns the current top stories from The Verge. It takes no parameters. Each item has its title, URL and, where available, a summary, author, publication time, image URL and 'type'. Use the headlines endpoint to read one section.

### `theverge_sections`

Get The Verge sections. Lists the The Verge sections that the headlines endpoint accepts: 'tech', 'reviews', 'science', 'entertainment', 'ai', 'policy', 'gaming', 'mobile', 'apps' and 'features'. Each entry has a 'slug', a display 'name' and a section 'url'.

### `thisismoney_article`

Get This Is Money article content. Returns one This Is Money article by 'url', a canonical HTTPS article link. The response has the title, description, section, authors, publication and update times, image URL, body 'paragraphs' and a 'paywalled' flag. Pages that are subscriber-only or blocked return an error.

### `thisismoney_author`

Get a This Is Money author profile. Returns a This Is Money author's profile by 'url', a canonical 'thisismoney.co.uk/profile-<id>/<slug>.html' link: name, job title, bio, coverage topic tags such as Money or Bills, and recent articles with title, URL, excerpt and ISO-8601 'published_at'. 'job_title' and 'coverage' can be empty.

### `thisismoney_headlines`

Get This Is Money section headlines. Returns the current headlines for one This Is Money section. 'section' is required and takes one of 'money', 'markets', 'investing', 'savings', 'pensions', 'mortgages', 'property', 'cars', 'travel' or 'consumer'. Each item has its title and URL, plus summary, author, publication time and image when the outlet provides them.

### `thisismoney_news`

Get This Is Money top stories. Returns the current top stories from This Is Money. It takes no parameters. Each item has its title, URL and, where available, a summary, author, publication time, image URL and 'type'. Use the headlines endpoint to read one section.

### `thisismoney_sections`

Get This Is Money sections. Lists the This Is Money sections that the headlines endpoint accepts, such as 'money', 'markets', 'savings', 'pensions', 'mortgages', 'property' and 'cars'. Each entry has a 'slug', a display 'name' and a section 'url'.

### `threads_post`

Retrieve a public Threads post. Returns one public Threads post by 'username' (with or without a leading '@') and the post 'code' from its URL. The response has the post text, canonical URL, preview image URL, and the author's id, name and username. Replies and logged-in fields are not included. An unavailable post returns 404.

### `threads_post_replies`

Retrieve public replies to a Threads post. Returns the public replies currently exposed to logged-out visitors. The response identifies when Threads reports additional replies but withholds a usable continuation cursor.

### `threads_profile`

Retrieve a public Threads profile. Returns a public Threads profile by 'username' (with or without a leading '@'): name, profile URL, biography, avatar URL, 'followers_count' and 'threads_count'. Counts are derived from the compact figures shown on the profile page. An unavailable profile returns 404.

### `threads_profile_media`

Retrieve public media posts from a Threads profile. Returns the first public page shown on a profile's Media tab. Items include image and video URLs, including carousel attachments, plus post and topic metadata. The logged-out page exposes no continuation cursor or media-type filter; 'pagination_limited' reports when additional results are gated by login or lack a supported cursor.

### `threads_profile_posts`

Retrieve public posts from a Threads profile. Lists public posts from the profile's Threads tab by 'username'. Each item has its code, URL, text, creation time, image and video URLs, like, reply, repost and quote counts, reply flag and author. When 'has_more' is true, pass 'next_cursor' unchanged as 'cursor' to fetch the next page; 'pagination_limited' is true if Threads withholds a usable cursor.

### `threads_profile_replies`

Retrieve public items from a Threads profile's Replies tab. Returns the first public page shown on a profile's Replies tab. Each item preserves its actual author and public reply metadata. The logged-out page has no continuation cursor; 'pagination_limited' is true when Threads reports more items without a cursor or shows a login wall for additional items.

### `threads_profile_reposts`

Retrieve public posts reposted by a Threads profile. Returns the first public page shown on a profile's Reposts tab. Each item preserves the original post author and metadata. 'pagination_limited' is true when Threads gates more items behind login or reports more items without a supported cursor.

### `threads_profile_topics`

Discover public topic tags on a Threads profile. Returns every topic tag listed on a public profile, including the numeric tag id and canonical 'name' to pass as 'q' to '/threads/search/topics'. Community topics include their community metadata.

### `threads_search`

Search public Threads posts. Returns the public first page of Threads search results for a query. 'sort' supports 'top' and 'recent'; 'pagination_limited' marks the logged-out login wall because search has no continuation cursor. Author and date filters in Threads require login and are not exposed here.

### `threads_topic_search`

Search posts for a public Threads topic tag. Returns the public first page of posts for a topic tag. Discover the required 'tag_id' and its canonical query 'name' from '/threads/profile/{username}/topics' or a post's 'topic' metadata. Topic results have no logged-out continuation cursor; 'pagination_limited' marks the login wall for more results.

### `ticketmaster_attraction`

Get a Ticketmaster attraction. Returns one Ticketmaster attraction (artist, team or other event entity) by numeric 'id': name, synopsis, image, URL, classification (segment, genre, sub-genre) and 'has_artist_video'. Past performance 'setlists' and 'setlist_source_url' appear only when available. An unknown attraction returns 404.

### `ticketmaster_attraction_events`

List an attraction's Ticketmaster events. Lists upcoming Ticketmaster events for the attraction with numeric 'id'. 'page' is zero-based, 0 to 49, default 0; 'sort' is 'relevance' or 'date' (default). Each event has title, start time, time zone, venue, attractions, presales, seat map and status flags such as 'sold_out' and 'cancelled'. The response gives 'total'.

### `ticketmaster_attraction_related`

List a Ticketmaster attraction's related attractions. Returns the "Fans Also Viewed" attractions shown on one attraction's own page. An attraction with no recommendation data returns a valid empty list.

### `ticketmaster_attraction_reviews`

List a Ticketmaster attraction's fan reviews. Lists fan reviews for the Ticketmaster attraction with numeric 'id', with its 'average_rating', 'best_rating', 'total' and Ticketmaster's own 'ai_review_summary'. Each review has a rating, title, text, nickname, city, venue and date. 'offset' runs 0 to 9995 (default 0); 'limit' runs 10 to 50 (default 10).

### `ticketmaster_discover_categories`

List Ticketmaster discover categories. Lists every current Concerts, Sports, Arts & Theater, and Family category with pagination. Section accepts 'all', 'concerts', 'sports', 'arts-theater', and 'family'.

### `ticketmaster_discover_category_events`

List events in a Ticketmaster discover category. Lists events in a Ticketmaster discover category, identified by 'category_id' from 'ticketmaster-discover-categories'. 'page' is zero-based, 0 to 49. Each event has title, start time, time zone, venue, attractions, presales, seat map and status flags such as 'sold_out' and 'cancelled'. The response gives 'total' and 'count'.

### `ticketmaster_discover_cities`

List Ticketmaster discover cities. Lists Ticketmaster's discover city destinations for a 'country' (two-letter code, default 'US'). Each city has a 'slug', name, canonical URL, locale and image. 'page' starts at 1 and 'per_page' runs 1 to 100. The response gives 'total'. Pass a city 'slug' to 'ticketmaster-discover-city-events'.

### `ticketmaster_discover_city_events`

List events in a Ticketmaster discover city. Lists events for a Ticketmaster discover city, identified by 'city' (a slug from 'ticketmaster-discover-cities') and 'country' (two-letter code matching the city, default 'US'). It covers all municipalities grouped under that destination. 'page' is zero-based, 0 to 49. Each event has title, start time, venue, attractions and status flags.

### `ticketmaster_event`

Get a Ticketmaster event. Returns one Ticketmaster event by 'id': title, description, start time, time zone, currency, venue, attractions, classification, presales, on-sale time, seat map URL, and flags for sold out, cancelled, postponed, rescheduled and virtual. An unknown event returns 404; a concluded or removed event returns 410.

### `ticketmaster_search_events`

Search Ticketmaster events. Searches Ticketmaster events by artist, event, team, or venue. A zero total with an empty events list is a valid no-results response. The sort enum accepts 'relevance' and 'date'.

### `ticketmaster_suggest`

Suggest Ticketmaster artists, events, and venues. Returns autocomplete suggestions for a partial artist, event, team or venue name in 'q'. Each suggestion has a title, 'type', category, URL, image and, when available, an 'event_count'. The response also gives the echoed 'query' and the 'count' of suggestions.

### `ticketmaster_trending_attractions`

List trending Ticketmaster attractions. Returns a ranked list of currently-trending attractions across every segment (music, sports, arts and theater, family), not scoped to one category or city.

### `ticketmaster_venue`

Get a Ticketmaster venue. Returns one Ticketmaster venue by numeric 'id': name, address, city, state, country, postal code, coordinates, time zone, image, URL and visitor information as name and text entries. 'seat_maps' and 'city_categories' are omitted when none exist. An unknown venue returns 404.

### `ticketmaster_venue_enhanced_details`

Get a Ticketmaster venue's enhanced branding details. Returns header branding imagery and external links (the venue's own site, resident teams) for major venues. Smaller venues without enhanced content return 404.

### `ticketmaster_venue_events`

List a venue's Ticketmaster events. Lists upcoming Ticketmaster events at the venue with numeric 'id'. 'page' is zero-based, 0 to 49, default 0; 'sort' is 'relevance' or 'date' (default). Each event has title, start time, time zone, attractions, presales, seat map and status flags such as 'sold_out' and 'cancelled'. The response gives 'total'.

### `ticketweb_event`

Get a TicketWeb event. Returns details for one TicketWeb event: venue, dates, age restriction, delivery methods, and per-tier ticket pricing (base price, fee breakdown, and total) when tickets are on sale. 'has_tickets' is false and 'sections' is empty for a free/RSVP event with no paid tickets, a sold-out event, or an access-code-gated event -- TicketWeb's own data does not reliably distinguish these three cases at this level, so the response reports the shared observable state (no purchasable sections) rather than guessing which applies.

### `ticketweb_search`

Search TicketWeb events. Searches TicketWeb events by artist, event, or venue. A zero count with an empty events list is a valid no-results response. availability is one of 'in_stock', 'sold_out', 'unknown' per event.

### `ticketweb_venue`

Get a TicketWeb venue. Returns one TicketWeb venue's detail (name, address) plus one page of its upcoming events. A zero count with an empty events list on page 1 is a valid "no upcoming events" response.

### `tiffany_categories`

List Tiffany & Co. categories. Lists every category id Tiffany & Co.'s own product catalog accepts, each with a human-readable label, a kind (category for a real navigable department/subcategory, curated_shop for a curated gift/merchandising shelf), and a live product count. Each id is exactly what tiffany-category's own category parameter accepts -- resolves the category-discovery gap that parameter would otherwise leave as "find one from a storefront URL".

### `tiffany_category`

Browse a Tiffany & Co. category. Returns one page of a Tiffany & Co. category/browse listing. category is a category id from tiffany-categories's own id field (e.g. ecommerce_us_jewelry_necklaces_and_pendants). sort selects recommended (default), price_asc, price_desc, or newest. material, gemstone, color, product_type, gender, and designer are optional single-value filters -- see tiffany-filters for the live covered value space for each. A hub-level or emptied-out category id, or a filter combination with no matches, returns a well-formed empty result rather than an error.

### `tiffany_content_search`

Search Tiffany & Co. editorial content. Searches Tiffany & Co.'s own editorial pages -- style guides, gift guides, and other "World of Tiffany" articles -- by free-text keyword. Not product data: no price, stock, or item id fields. A genuine non-matching keyword returns a well-formed empty result (zero total_results).

### `tiffany_filters`

List Tiffany & Co. search/category filter values. Lists every value tiffany-search's and tiffany-category's material, gemstone, color, product_type, gender, and designer filter parameters accept, each with a live product count -- resolves the discovery gap those parameters would otherwise leave as "find one on the live site's own filter sidebar".

### `tiffany_product`

Get a Tiffany & Co. product. Returns full product detail for one item: name, description, brand, collection, designer, material, gemstone, USD price, live stock status, category tree, every color/style variation, and images. product_id is Tiffany & Co.'s own item id, as returned by tiffany-search's or tiffany-category's own products[].id field.

### `tiffany_search`

Search Tiffany & Co. products. Searches Tiffany & Co.'s product catalog by free-text keyword. Returns product summaries with USD pricing, live stock status, material, gemstone, collection, and designer. sort selects recommended (default), price_asc, price_desc, or newest. material, gemstone, color, product_type, gender, and designer are optional single-value filters -- see tiffany-filters for the live covered value space for each. A genuine non-matching keyword, or a filter combination with no matches, returns a well-formed empty result (zero total_products).

### `tiffany_stores`

Find Tiffany & Co. store locations. Finds Tiffany & Co. physical stores, boutiques, and cafes near a coordinate, ordered by distance. Each result includes address, phone, opening hours, in-store services and specialities, and live open/closed status.

### `tiffany_suggest`

Get Tiffany & Co. search-box suggestions. Returns Tiffany & Co.'s own search-box suggestions (typeahead) for a partial query -- a flat list of suggested search phrases, each with its own live total result count on the product catalog. Not product data.

### `tiktok_category`

List TikTok explore categories. Returns the content categories shown on TikTok's Explore page. Each entry has the category name and its numeric type code. Takes no parameters.

### `tiktok_challenge`

Retrieve TikTok hashtag details. Returns the details of a TikTok hashtag page by 'name', for example 'christmas'. The response carries 'challengeInfo' with the hashtag's metadata, such as cover images, and 'shareMeta' with the share title and description. The hashtag id found here feeds 'tiktok-challenge-list'.

### `tiktok_challenge_list`

Retrieve TikTok hashtag posts. Lists the videos posted under a TikTok hashtag, identified by the hashtag 'id' from the hashtag detail endpoint. 'cursor' defaults to 0. The response has 'itemList', 'hasMore' and a 'cursor'; pass that cursor back to fetch the next page.

### `tiktok_comments`

Retrieve TikTok video comments. Returns the top-level comments on a TikTok video, by the video id from its URL ('aweme_id'). Results are paged by cursor: pass the 'cursor' from one response to get the next page, and read 'has_more' to see whether more remain. The response also carries the total comment count.

### `tiktok_creative_center_filters`

Retrieve TikTok Creative Center filter taxonomy. Returns the complete filter taxonomy for the Creative Center trend endpoints: the countries each trend tab reports, the industry ids and video content tags the filters accept, the supported lookback periods, and the video sort metrics. Use it to discover valid values for the hashtags endpoint's country_code, period, and industry_id parameters and the videos endpoint's country_code, period, sort_by, and content_label_ids parameters. This endpoint performs no upstream request and has no parameters.

### `tiktok_creative_center_hashtags`

Retrieve TikTok Creative Center trending hashtags. Returns TikTok Creative Center's ranked trending hashtags for a country, period, and optional industry. TikTok gates this endpoint's full result set behind a logged-in TikTok One account: an anonymous request always receives at most 3 hashtags per filter combination regardless of country, period, or industry, so selecting an industry returns that industry's own ranked top three. See the filters endpoint for the complete country, period, and industry value lists.

### `tiktok_creative_center_top_content`

Retrieve TikTok Creative Center top content. Returns TikTok Creative Center's current Top Content set: four top-performing branded videos, each with the video object (anonymous MP4 and cover URLs), engagement metrics, the author profile and follower count, and (by default) the video's top comments plus keyword mention counts derived from them. The set is a daily snapshot and there is no pagination or historical query; the four titles rotate when the snapshot changes. Set include_comments=false for a smaller response with only video, author, and metrics.

### `tiktok_creative_center_videos`

Retrieve TikTok Creative Center trending videos. Returns TikTok Creative Center's ranked trending videos for a country, period, sort order, and optional content tags. TikTok reports the true result-set size (see total_count/page_count in the response) but gates access to it behind a logged-in TikTok One account: an anonymous request always receives page 1 (4 videos) regardless of sort order or period. Country coverage is uneven: only US, JP, ID, VN, and TH have a regional edge host that returns populated results; other countries return an empty videos array (a genuine no-data response, not an error). See the filters endpoint for the complete country, period, sort, and content tag value lists.

### `tiktok_explore`

Retrieve the TikTok explore feed for a category. Returns the TikTok explore feed for a category, given its category type 'id' from the category endpoint. The response has 'itemList' with the videos, 'hasMore' and a 'cursor'. A feed that comes back empty is reported as an upstream error, not as an empty list.

### `tiktok_mobile_anchor_list`

Anchor catalogue used by the video composer. Returns the anchor catalogue TikTok exposes for attaching a tag, product or place to a video. Entry shapes vary by anchor type, so each entry is returned as raw JSON rather than coerced into one schema.

### `tiktok_mobile_comment_replies`

Retrieve replies to a TikTok comment. Returns the replies to one comment as the mobile app returns them, with 'cursor', 'has_more' and 'total'. The measured call sends both the video id and the comment id; this route answers even in windows where the top-level comment list is degraded.

### `tiktok_mobile_comments`

Retrieve comments for a TikTok video. Returns the top-level comments of one video as the mobile app returns them: each comment has its full 'user' projection, 'text', 'digg_count' and 'reply_comment_total', plus 'cursor', 'has_more' and 'total'. This route needs a signed-in app session and throttles independently of the replies route. A page with no comments (including an empty body) is returned as an empty result, because that is the documented degraded shape in a throttle window.

### `tiktok_mobile_feed`

Retrieve the TikTok mobile For You feed. Returns one page of videos from TikTok's mobile For You feed, signed with well-formed mobile signature headers (no device or account needed). Each item carries 'aweme_id', 'create_time', 'author_id', 'share_url' and the verified statistics block ('play_count', 'digg_count', 'comment_count', 'share_count', 'collect_count', 'download_count', 'forward_count', 'lose_count', 'lose_comment_count', 'whatsapp_share_count', 'repost_count'). A zero 'count' uses the app's default page size; 'count' is capped at 50.

### `tiktok_mobile_feed_post`

Fetch the app's primary feed call (POST, protobuf) decoded without a schema. Calls the app's primary feed route - 'POST /aweme/v2/feed/', which the Android client sends with a protobuf request body and answers with protobuf - and returns a schema-free decode: field numbers become keys, length-delimited fields become strings when printable, nested messages when they parse and base64 otherwise, plus a flat list of every string leaf. Field numbering is inferred because TikTok publishes no schema for this message; use the JSON 'GET /tiktok/mobile/feed' route when you need the stable structured contract.

### `tiktok_mobile_hashtag`

Retrieve a TikTok hashtag. Returns one hashtag's detail by name: 'challenge_info' (cid, hashtag_name, desc, ...) and 'stats' (view and video counts), exactly as the mobile API returns them. Hashtags are addressed by name; an internal id is rejected upstream.

### `tiktok_mobile_hashtag_posts`

Retrieve videos for a TikTok hashtag. Lists videos for one hashtag name as the mobile app returns them ('aweme_list' with author, music and statistics), plus 'cursor' and 'has_more'. 'sort=fresh' is the newest list and works from any measured egress; 'sort=popular' is the hot list and only answers from a US egress.

### `tiktok_mobile_hashtags`

Search TikTok hashtags. Searches hashtags by keyword and returns the matching hashtag objects unmodified, with 'cursor' and 'has_more' for paging.

### `tiktok_mobile_live_effects`

Retrieve TikTok LIVE effects. Returns the complete LIVE effects/sticker asset catalogue in one call: 'data.assets' (2,032 assets, each with 'id', 'name', 'describe', 'resource_url', 'resource_uri', 'md5', 'size', 'resource_type', 'download_type', 'model_requirements', 'sticker_asset_variant' and 'video_resource_list'). There are no request parameters and no paging, and the body is large because the catalogue is complete.

### `tiktok_mobile_live_gifts`

Retrieve TikTok LIVE gifts. Returns the complete LIVE gift catalogue in one call: 'data.gifts' (771 gift objects with 'diamond_count', 'describe', 'duration', 'gift_resources', 'gift_skins', 'batch_gift_info' and 'combo') plus the gift config and resource maps ('gift_configs', 'gifts_info', 'doodle_templates', 'gift_name_group_map', 'gift_resource_group_map'). There are no request parameters and no paging: the response is a single complete catalogue.

### `tiktok_mobile_live_hashtags`

LIVE category/game reference catalogue (hashtags, live-studio/voice/third-party tags, game tags). Returns the reference set the app's "go LIVE" flow uses to tag a stream: the general LIVE hashtags ('hashtags', measured 18 entries of '{id, image, namespace, title}', where 'id' 0 is the "None" tag), the live-studio/live-voice/third-party hashtag subsets ('live_studio_hashtags' 16, 'live_voice_hashtags' 16, 'third_party_hashtags' 9), the single 'game_hashtag', and a 1,500-entry game catalogue ('game_tag_list', 'game_tag_count') where every entry carries the same 12 keys: 'id', 'short_name', 'show_name', 'full_name', 'bundle_id', 'package_name', 'game_category' ('[{game_type, title}]' with PC games/Mobile games/Console games/Others), 'hashtag_id', 'hashtag_list', 'gar', 'landscape' (0/1/2) and 'is_new_game'. The upstream is '/webcast/room/hashtag/list/' on the webcast edge host (no origin header); the measured body is 539,361 B and byte-identical on both working webcast hosts, 'language'/'count' do not change it, and there is no cursor/has_more, so it is a one-shot reference dump. Measured 2026-10-22 with the pure-Go (device-free) signer, so it does not need the device-backed signer.

### `tiktok_mobile_live_room`

LIVE room detail: status, viewers, owner, stream URLs, cover. Returns one LIVE room's detail, keyed by 'room_id' — the numeric id that '/api/v1/tiktok/mobile/live/search' returns under 'data[].lives.author.room_id'. The upstream is '/webcast/room/info/' on the webcast edge host (no origin header), captured from the running 47.4.3 app's LIVE surface and reproduced against the live gateway. The response projects the fields callers key on — 'title', 'status' (2 = live), 'user_count' (concurrent viewers), 'create_time', 'owner' (user id, nickname, avatar), 'stats' (cumulative 'enter_count'/'total_user', 'watch_user_count', 'like_count', 'comment_count', 'share_count', 'follow_count', 'replay_viewers'), 'stream' (playable 'flv_pull_url' per resolution plus 'default_resolution'/'candidate_resolution' and the HLS/RTMP URLs) and 'cover' — and keeps the upstream room object unmodified in 'data' (it has ~500 keys, so a partial struct would drop fields). Measured 2026-10-22 with the pure-Go (device-free) signer: one room returned 193-198 KB with 1,595-1,600 concurrent viewers, 27,916 cumulative viewers, 27,096 enters and FLV URLs for FULL_HD1/HD1/SD1/SD2. 'anchor_id' is deliberately NOT forwarded: it was measured to suppress the audience-only 'stats.total_user' (27,916 -> 0 on the same room). A missing, non-numeric or unknown room id answers the webcast envelope's status 10011 and is surfaced as a 400; a finished room (status 30003) is a 400 too. The route is not signature-gated, so it does not need the device-backed signer.

### `tiktok_mobile_live_room_by_user`

LIVE room by user: the room a user is currently streaming. Returns the LIVE room a TikTok user is currently streaming, keyed by 'user_id'. The upstream is '/webcast/room/info_by_user/' on the webcast edge host (no origin header) and returns the same room payload as '/api/v1/tiktok/mobile/live/room' (title, status, concurrent viewers, owner, cumulative stats, per-resolution FLV URLs, cover and the ~500-key room object in 'data'), except that the caller addresses a user and the room id is filled from the payload (both 'user_id' and 'room_id' are echoed). Measured 2026-10-22 with the pure-Go (device-free) signer: 'user_id=6707748031095751686' answered 184,575 B (195,220 B on the second webcast host); 'anchor_id' alone answers a 57-byte empty payload, so 'user_id' is the address. A user with no live room answers status 30003 "room has finished" and is surfaced as a 400; a non-numeric user id is a 400 (status 10011); a bare call answers a 57-byte empty success envelope, which is why this endpoint requires 'user_id'. The route is not signature-gated, so it does not need the device-backed signer.

### `tiktok_mobile_live_search`

Search TikTok LIVE streams. Searches the mobile app's LIVE surface by keyword: 'data' of '{type, anchor}' entries with 'feedback_type' set to 'live', plus 'cursor' and 'has_more'. 'keyword' is required; without it the gateway answers a valid but empty envelope. This is the API's first LIVE endpoint.

### `tiktok_mobile_live_tabs`

Fetch the LIVE tab catalogue. Returns the app's LIVE tab catalogue: 'data[]' holds one entry per tab with the tab's 'id', 'name', 'style', 'enable'/'event' flags and the exact 'url'/'inter_url' feed template the client calls for that tab. The measured tab 1 ("live") points at '/webcast/feed/?content_type=0&style=2&channel_id=21&sub_channel_id=0&tab_id=1&type=live&sub_type=live&req_type=0&cate_id=0' on 'webcast.tiktokv.com'. This closes the route round 553 could not find a host for; it is served by the webcast edge hosts (non-webcast hosts answer 403) and is one of the few LIVE routes that answers device-free: measured with the pure-Go placeholder signer as well as the real device signer, so it does not need the device-backed signing service.

### `tiktok_mobile_music_beats`

Retrieve TikTok music beats. Returns the mobile app's beats/songs chart unmodified: 'music_list' of the same full sound objects the pick chart returns ('id_str', 'title', 'user_count', 'album', 'artists', 'cover_*'), ordered as the app's beats list. The measured envelope carries no paging fields.

### `tiktok_mobile_music_choices`

Recommended sounds for video creation. Returns the app's "music choices" list: the recommended sounds it offers on the video-creation page. The upstream is '/aweme/v1/music/choices/'; each 'music_list' entry is the same full sound object the chart routes return (title, album, artists, covers, play URL, duration, ...). Measured 2026-10-21 with the pure-Go (device-free) signer: 56,078 B / 6 full sound objects on one call and 7 on later calls (the same six at the front), and the payload carries NO paging fields (no cursor/has_more), so this is a one-shot recommendation list. The measured 'item_id', 'music_id', 'count' and 'scene' parameters did not deterministically change the list — the recommendations rotate — so none is exposed. The route is not signature-gated, so it does not need the device-backed signer.

### `tiktok_mobile_music_collection_list`

Music collection list (paged browse). Returns the app's music-collection LIST ('mc_list' of collection objects with covers), the browse list of curated music collections. This is a different route from '/api/v1/tiktok/mobile/music/collections', which is the collection FEED ('mcf_list', with each entry's music inline). The upstream is '/aweme/v1/music/collection/'. Unlike the feed, this route PAGES for real: 'count' is honoured (measured 1 -> 1 item with 'cursor: 1, has_more: 1'; 5 -> 5 items with 'cursor: 5'; 10/100 -> all 8 collections) and 'cursor' advances (measured 'count=5&cursor=5' -> the remaining 3 with 'has_more: 0'). A negative count answers upstream status 5, which is rejected locally. Measured 2026-10-21 with the pure-Go (device-free) signer: 8 collections total. The route is not signature-gated, so it does not need the device-backed signer.

### `tiktok_mobile_music_collections`

Retrieve TikTok music collections. Returns the mobile app's sound-collection feed unmodified: 'mcf_list', where each entry is '{collection, music_list}' (the measured default page holds 8 entries), plus 'cursor' and 'has_more'. This route is first-page only: the returned 'cursor' is not a reusable page token, so callers should not page with it.

### `tiktok_mobile_music_pick`

Retrieve TikTok sound chart picks. Returns the mobile app's sound pick/chart list: 'music_list' of full sound objects (id, title, author, user_count, duration, ...) plus the chart list 'mc_list' and 'radio_cursor'.

### `tiktok_mobile_music_posts`

Retrieve videos for a TikTok sound. Lists the videos that use one sound, as the mobile app returns them: 'aweme_list' of full video objects (with 'author', 'statistics' and 'added_sound_music_info'), plus 'cursor' and 'has_more'. 'music_id' is required. 'count' is accepted but ignored upstream - the server returns its own default page, so page with 'cursor'.

### `tiktok_mobile_music_related`

Retrieve sounds related to a TikTok video. Returns sounds related to one video: 'music_list' of full sound objects, 'recall_info_list' explaining why each was recalled, 'similar_song_ids', plus 'cursor' and 'has_more'.

### `tiktok_mobile_music_trending`

Retrieve TikTok trending sounds. Returns the mobile app's trending sound chart: 'music_list' of full sound objects ('id_str', 'title', 'user_count', 'album', 'artists', 'cover_large'/'cover_medium'/'cover_thumb', 'binded_challenge_id', 'collect_stat', 'audition_duration') unmodified, plus 'cursor' and 'has_more' for paging. This is the chart behind 'music.trending'.

### `tiktok_mobile_mv_videos`

MV channel feed: the app's music-video tab, paged. Returns one page of an MV channel feed, the app's music-video ("MV") tab. The upstream is '/aweme/v1/mv/aweme/'; 'mv_id' is a small numeric CHANNEL index, NOT a video id — measured ids 0-10 each returned a 15-video page of full aweme objects (1.05-1.24 MB), while 100 returned a valid empty page and a real aweme id returned an empty list. The server's page size is 15 and 'count' was measured IGNORED ('count=5' and 'count=10' both returned 15 items), so 'count' is not exposed; page with 'cursor'. The returned 'cursor' is a reusable next-page token (measured page 1 'cursor: 18, has_more: 1'; 'cursor=18' returned a fresh page with 'cursor: 38, has_more: 1'). The envelope's 'top_awemes' (pinned entries), 'original_aweme_id', 'page_extra' and 'extra'/'log_pb' are kept as measured. Measured 2026-10-22 with the pure-Go (device-free) signer, so it does not need the device-backed signer. A missing or non-numeric 'mv_id' is a 400; an unknown numeric channel is a valid empty page.

### `tiktok_mobile_place_detail`

Place (POI) detail from the mobile app's Places surface. Returns one place detail page, keyed by the 'poi_id' that the place search endpoint returns. The upstream is TikTok's server-driven UI ('/tiktok/poi/slash/v1') frame stream, assembled here into the component map of the place-detail screen: 'food_head_info' (place name, formatted address, category, phone, coordinates, opening hours, rating/score with mention count, price range, tags and photo album), 'poi_top_videos' (top videos strip), 'poi_limited_post' (posts about the place: full video items plus 'aweme_cursor'/'has_more_aweme'), 'poi_review' (review preview with 'has_more') and 'ai_summary' when the place has one. 'nodes' is opaque and complete, 'frames' keeps the raw ordered frames, and the typed counters ('top_video_count', 'post_count', 'post_cursor', 'has_more_posts', 'review_count', 'has_more_reviews') are convenience projections. The measured page-size controls are forwarded with the app's defaults but the server applies its own bounds. The route is not signature-gated, so it does not need the device-backed signer.

### `tiktok_mobile_place_info`

Compact place (POI) record: address, coordinates, rating, hours, counters. Returns one place's compact record, keyed by the 'poi_id' that the place search endpoint returns. The upstream is TikTok's POI read ('/tiktok/poi/get/v1'), the record behind a place card: 'name', 'address', 'category', 'average_price', 'latitude'/'longitude', 'city_code'/'region_code', 'review_score' with 'review_count'/'no_rating', 'video_count', 'favorite_count', 'opening_hours'/'opening_status', 'cover', 'share_url'/'share_desc' and 'parent_poi', plus the upstream POI object unmodified in 'place' so a richer field is never lost. This is the cheap lookup to use instead of the ~1 MB slash detail page when only the place record is needed. A nonexistent id answers 400 (the upstream business status 3009009 "poi not exist" is a caller error, not an outage). Measured 2026-10-21 with the pure-Go (device-free) signer: 4,594 B for a coffee shop (score 4.7 / 2 reviews, price "$", hours "8:00 AM – 5:00 PM", 11 videos), 4,623 B for a second location (score 4.8 / 13 reviews). The route is not signature-gated, so it does not need the device-backed signer.

### `tiktok_mobile_place_photos`

Place photo album with per-photo attribution. Returns one place's photo album, keyed by the 'poi_id' that the place search endpoint returns. The upstream is '/tiktok/poi/picture_album/v1': 'categories' holds each album tab ('name', 'pic_tab_typecode', 'pictures' of bare image URL lists and 'pictures_v2', the same photos with 'author' attribution, 'pic_id', 'source' and origin/compressed URL info), 'photo_count' sums the categories' pictures, and 'title' is the app's own header. Measured 2026-10-21 with the pure-Go (device-free) signer: one place answered 5,368 B, title "Gallery (3)", 1 category with 3 photos whose 'pictures_v2' entries name the Google-places contributor; another answered 24,196 B with more photos. The album is one-shot: 'count' and 'pic_tab_typecode' were measured and did not change the page. A nonexistent id answers 500 (the upstream answers status 4 "Server is currently unavailable" on this route, unlike the poi-not-exist code the other place routes use). The route is not signature-gated, so it does not need the device-backed signer.

### `tiktok_mobile_place_videos`

Videos posted at one place (paged). Returns one page of the videos posted at a place, keyed by the 'poi_id' that the place search endpoint returns. The upstream is '/tiktok/poi/video/list/v1': 'aweme_list' holds the app's full video objects (id, description, author, statistics, media URLs, music, anchors, ...) and 'item_count' is this page's size. Page with 'cursor': the returned 'cursor' is a reusable next-page token (measured page 1 'cursor: 20' with 'has_more: 1', page 2 'cursor: 40'), never with arithmetic on 'count'. 'count' is a page-size hint, not a strict size: 1/2/5 returned exactly that many items on the first page, a later page returned 8 for count=5, and 10/20/50 were all server-capped at 17. Measured 2026-10-21 with the pure-Go (device-free) signer: 11 videos (940-944 KB) on one place, 17 videos (1.4 MB) on another. The route exposes no sort control: 'sort_type' and 'order' were measured and did not change the page or its order. The upstream throttles bursts, so paced clients are expected. The route is not signature-gated, so it does not need the device-backed signer.

### `tiktok_mobile_search`

Search TikTok videos on the mobile API. Keyword search returning the mobile API result documents unmodified: each entry has 'aweme_info' (a full video object with statistics), 'card_profile' and search metadata, plus 'cursor' and 'has_more'. Keep 'count' small (20 already exceeds one megabyte of upstream JSON). Requires the device-backed signing service; without it the endpoint returns a generic service-unavailable error instead of an empty page.

### `tiktok_mobile_search_effects`

Search TikTok effects/stickers by keyword. Searches TikTok's effect catalogue by 'keyword', returning the app's full effect objects ('name', 'hint', 'icon_url', 'file_url', 'effect_id', 'types', 'tags', 'parent'/'children', 'effect_type', 'music', 'source', 'designer_id', 'schema'). The upstream is '/aweme/v1/search/effect/'; the page is unfolded to the top level ('effects', 'cursor', 'has_more', 'search_id', 'use_hot', plus 'bind_effects'/'collection' on some queries). Paging is real but needs BOTH halves of the token: pass the previous response's 'cursor' and 'search_id' together (measured: page 1 'cursor: 100', page 2 with 'cursor=100&search_id=...' returned the final effect with 'has_more: false'; a cursor without its 'search_id' returns an empty page, which the service rejects as a 400). 'count' and 'offset' were measured as no-ops. Measured 2026-10-21 with the pure-Go (device-free) signer: 'keyword=green screen' -> 6 effects (11,831 B) + 1 on page 2, 'green' -> 2, '字幕' -> 4; a keyword with no matches is a valid empty page. The route is not signature-gated, so it does not need the device-backed signer.

### `tiktok_mobile_search_hashtags`
